units.source_text: "南泉斩猫吗？"

en.t: "Was it Nanquan cutting the cat?"

units.source_text: 柏木比了比木贼草的长度，尔后一边往水盘里插花一边回答说：

en.t: Kashiwagi compared the lengths of the horsetail reeds, then answered while arranging the flowers in the water basin:

units.source_text: "那桩公案嘛，在人的一生中是经常变形的，而且以各种形态多次出现。

en.t: "That koan, you see, keeps changing shape throughout a person's life, and appears many times in many different forms.

units.source_text: 那是一桩令人毛骨悚然的公案哩。

en.t: It is a truly hair-raising koan.

units.source_text: 每次我们在人生的拐角处相会的时候，都改变着同一公案的面貌和意义。

en.t: Every time we meet it at a turning point in life, the same koan changes its face and its meaning.

units.source_text: 南泉和尚所斩的猫原来就是精于艺能的。

en.t: The cat that Priest Nanquan cut down was, from the start, skilled in the arts.

units.source_text: 猫很漂亮。

en.t: The cat was beautiful.

units.source_text: 你知道，简直是漂亮无比哩。

en.t: You know, it was simply beautiful beyond compare.

units.source_text: 猫眼是金色的，长毛光洁可爱，躯体小巧而柔软，这个世界的所有逸乐和美似乎都像弹簧似地缩藏在它的躯体里。

en.t: Its eyes were golden, its long fur glossy and lovely, and its body small and soft; all the pleasures and beauty of this world seemed compressed inside it like a spring.

units.source_text: 除了我，几乎所有注释者都忘记说：猫原来就是美的凝聚体。

en.t: Almost every commentator except me has forgotten to say this: the cat was, from the beginning, a condensation of beauty itself.

units.source_text: 可是，这猫简直故意似的突然从草丛中跳出来，闪烁着优美而狡黠的目光。

en.t: But this cat suddenly leapt out of the grass as if on purpose, its graceful and cunning eyes flashing.

units.source_text: 它被逮住了。

en.t: It was caught.

units.source_text: 这就是造成两堂相争的根源。

en.t: This was the root cause of the dispute between the two halls.

units.source_text: 为什么呢？

en.t: Why was that?

units.source_text: 因为美可以委身于任何人，但又不属于任何人。

en.t: Because beauty can give itself to anyone, yet belongs to no one.

units.source_text: 所谓美这种东西，是啊，怎么说才好呢？

en.t: This thing called beauty, well, how should I put it?

units.source_text: 它好比龋齿，疼痛，触及舌头，株连舌头，强调自己的存在。

en.t: It is like a decayed tooth: it aches, touches the tongue, drags the tongue into it, and insists on its own existence.

units.source_text: 人终于忍受不了痛楚而清牙医把它拔掉。

en.t: At last a person can no longer endure the pain and has a dentist pull it out.

units.source_text: 把沾满血的、茶色的、肮脏的小龋齿放在掌心上看过之后，可能会这样说：

en.t: After looking at the small, bloodstained, brown, filthy decayed tooth lying in the palm, one might say:

units.source_text: 是这个吗？

en.t: Was it this?

units.source_text: 原来就是这个家伙吗？

en.t: Was it this thing all along?

units.source_text: 它给我带来痛苦，不断地让我恼于它的存在，于是在我的体内顽固地扎下了根，如今它只不过是死了的物质而已。

en.t: It brought me pain, constantly tormented me with its presence, and stubbornly sank roots inside my body, yet now it is nothing but dead matter.

units.source_text: 但是那个和这个真的是同样的东西吗？

en.t: But are that thing and this thing really the same?

units.source_text: 倘使这个本来就是我的外部存在，那么它为什么又能以什么因缘来联结我的内部，成为我的痛苦的根源呢？

en.t: If this was originally something outside me, then why, and by what connection, could it link itself to my inside and become the source of my pain?

units.source_text: 这东西存在的根据是什么呢？

en.t: What is the ground for this thing's existence?

units.source_text: 它的根据难道就是在我的内部吗？

en.t: Could its ground really be inside me?

units.source_text: 抑或在它本身呢？

en.t: Or is it in the thing itself?

units.source_text: 尽管如此，我来把它拔掉，放在我的掌心上，这绝对是别的东西。

en.t: Even so, when I pull it out and place it in my palm, this is absolutely something else.

units.source_text: 断然不是它。"

en.t: It is certainly not that."
